newsitem.title: USA: Federated Stores to expand private brands.
newsitem.headline: Federated Stores to expand private brands.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc said Tuesday it plans to continue to expand its private brands merchandise program in efforts to increase both comparable store sales and earnings in 1997.
It also plans to build stronger vendor partnerships and to continue to cut costs, all part of its strategies, it said.

"Federated's primary objective for 1997 is to focus on the aggressive execution of our current strategies, with the goal of producing comp-store sales growth and further improving our earnings performance," chairman and chief executive officer Allen Questrom said in the retailer's year-end statement.
Federated has 400-plus department stores and 150 specialty stores in 36 states. They include Bloomingdale's, Bon Marche, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Macy's, Rich's and Stern's.

Net sales of $15.23 billion in the year ended February 1 rose 1.2 percent from the previous year. For the quarter, sales fell 4.4 percent. However, 26 Broadway stores operated in the earlier year have closed or been sold and the earlier year and quarter included an extra week's results, Federated said.
Comparable-store sales for the 13-week quarter rose 4.0 percent from the first 13 weeks of last year's 14-week period.
For the year, comparable-store sales rose 3.1 percent compared with the first 52 weeks of 1995.

For the year, operating income rose 22.3 percent over the previous year, excluding non-recurring costs in both years related to the integration of R.H. Macy & Co and Broadway Stores Inc. Operating income rose 5.6 percent in the quarter excluding the adjustments.
Federated reported net income of $1.39 a share in the 13-week fourth quarter ended February 1 versus $1.21 a year ago in a 14-week period.
Excluding the inventory valuation adjustments and other business integration and consolidation expenses, it earned $1.65 a share before-tax against $1.46 a year ago, it said.

For the 52-week year, Federated earned $1.28 a share compared with 1995's 53-week sum of $0.39. Excluding the same item and a $25.6 million charitable contribution last year, it earned $2.18 versus $1.40.

Questrom said Federated believes its performance in the 52-week year versus the 53-week year "reflects our ability to successfully integrate major acquisitions while continuing to improve performance in our existing stores."
